title: Dictionary Training
description: Trains zstd dictionaries on representative samples so small messages compress like large ones. A shared dictionary captures the common substrings of a protocol — JSON keys, log prefixes — and each small payload references it. It routinely doubles compression ratios on small records.
key_mechanisms: Ship the dictionary with the codec

demo.title: Demo — Dictionary Training

title: Content-Type Detection
description: Sniffs the content type and picks brotli for HTML, zstd for JSON, and nothing for already-compressed data. Compressing a JPEG wastes CPU for zero gain; detecting the type first avoids it. The detector runs on magic bytes and headers, not file extensions.

demo.title: Demo — Content-Type Detection

title: Zstd Level Tuning
description: Sweeps compression levels 1 through 19 to find the knee of the ratio-versus-speed curve for each dataset. Level 3 is fast, level 19 squeezes hard, and the right choice depends on whether the data is read once or a million times. The tuner re-runs when data characteristics drift.
key_mechanisms: Find the knee of the ratio/speed curve

demo.title: Demo — Zstd Level Tuning

title: Brotli for Text
description: Uses brotli at quality 11 for static text assets served with long cache TTLs. Maximum-quality brotli beats gzip by 15 to 25 percent on HTML, CSS, and JS, and precompression means the CPU cost is paid once. It is the standard for static web assets.
key_mechanisms: Fall back to gzip for old clients

demo.title: Demo — Brotli for Text

title: Columnar Encoding Selection
description: Chooses run-length encoding for runs, dictionary encoding for low-cardinality columns, and delta encoding for sorted integers — per column. The selector profiles each column's value distribution and picks the encoding with the best ratio. Getting this right is what makes columnar formats fast.
key_mechanisms: Re-evaluate on schema or data change

demo.title: Demo — Columnar Encoding Selection

title: Image Format Selection
description: Serves AVIF where supported, WebP as fallback, and JPEG last, negotiated by Accept headers. Modern formats halve file sizes at the same quality, which is the single biggest lever on page weight. The selector runs at the edge so origins store one master.
key_mechanisms: Keep one master at the origin

demo.title: Demo — Image Format Selection

title: Video Codec Ladder
description: Encodes an H.264 baseline plus HEVC and AV1 renditions for adaptive streaming. Players pick the best codec their device supports at each bandwidth step. The ladder trades encoding cost for bandwidth savings across the device fleet.
key_mechanisms: Encode baseline H.264 plus modern renditions
Expose codec choices in the manifest
Let players pick per bandwidth step

demo.title: Demo — Video Codec Ladder

title: Entropy Estimation
description: Measures Shannon entropy of a sample to decide whether compression is worthwhile. High-entropy data like encrypted blobs cannot compress; the estimator skips them before wasting CPU. It is a cheap gate in front of every compression decision.
key_mechanisms: Skip compression above the entropy threshold

demo.title: Demo — Entropy Estimation

title: Pre-Compression Dedup
description: Deduplicates chunks before compressing so repeated data is compressed once. Content-defined chunking finds repeated segments across files, and the compressor only sees unique bytes. The combination beats either technique alone.

demo.title: Demo — Pre-Compression Dedup

title: Streaming vs Block Choice
description: Uses streaming mode for pipes and block mode for random access. Streaming compresses an unbounded flow with constant memory; block mode compresses independent chunks that can be decompressed in any order. The choice follows the access pattern.

demo.title: Demo — Streaming vs Block Choice

title: Hardware Offload Selection
description: Routes compression to QAT or NVMe offload engines when available, falling back to CPU otherwise. Hardware engines compress gigabytes per second without touching CPU cores. The selector probes for engines at startup and routes accordingly.
key_mechanisms: Probe for offload engines at startup

demo.title: Demo — Hardware Offload Selection

title: Compression Benchmark Harness
description: Continuously re-benchmarks codecs on production samples to catch drift in the optimal choice. Data changes — new log formats, new schemas — and the best codec changes with it. The harness alerts when a different codec wins by a margin.

demo.title: Demo — Compression Benchmark Harness

title: Adaptive Chunk Sizing
description: Grows chunk size for compressible data and shrinks it for random data. Large chunks compress better but waste work on incompressible bytes; the sizer adapts from recent ratios. It keeps throughput high across mixed streams.
key_mechanisms: Grow chunks when ratios are good

demo.title: Demo — Adaptive Chunk Sizing

title: Sparse Data Handling
description: Stores sparse columns as index-value pairs instead of dense arrays. When 99 percent of values are zero or null, dense storage wastes nearly everything; sparse encoding stores only what exists. Query engines skip the gaps without materializing them.

demo.title: Demo — Sparse Data Handling

title: Re-Compression Pipelines
description: Recompresses old archives with newer codecs during idle windows. A 2015 gzip archive becomes a 2025 zstd archive at half the size, paying back storage costs. The pipeline verifies byte-identical output before replacing originals.

demo.title: Demo — Re-Compression Pipelines
